purpose: SPEC-TRACK3B1-IDENTITY-PROMOTION-CORE changes crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs so that two genuinely distinct packages sharing a bare name across different ecosystems, at different paths, are promoted to PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem, name} and coexist as distinct registered packages, instead of hard-failing with GraphError::DuplicatePackage as they always have historically. Before that change, PackageId::name() collisions across two or more registered packages in the same workspace were structurally impossible -- the walker's DuplicatePackage rejection was the invariant every downstream PackageId::name()-keyed consumer implicitly relied on. Once SPEC-TRACK3B1 ships, that invariant is false, and two consumers in crates/callisto-graph currently key or filter exclusively by PackageId::name() (the bare name string, stripped of any ecosystem qualifier): `callisto matrix`'s report generator (crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs's build_matrix_report, and its --package filter in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs) and `callisto publish`'s --only filter (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs). This spec makes both consumers collision-safe: `callisto matrix` keys its BTreeMap report output by PackageId::display_name() (ecosystem-qualified) instead of the bare name, so two promoted siblings no longer silently overwrite each other's map entry, and both consumers' name-based filters (`--package`, `--only`) become ambiguity-aware, returning GraphError::AmbiguousName for a bare name that matches two or more promoted siblings instead of silently matching (and, for `--only`, silently publishing) all of them. This spec does not implement the identity-promotion mechanism itself (SPEC-TRACK3B1's job) -- it exists solely to eliminate the exact silent-corruption window SPEC-TRACK3B1's own non_goals section names as the reason a second spec is required: `callisto matrix` producing a report that silently drops one promoted sibling's platform/runtime data, and `callisto publish --only <name>` silently publishing a package the operator did not intend to release, both to live registries in CI, with no error and no diagnostic. SPEC-TRACK3B1's own non_goals section states this deployment-ordering constraint verbatim and marks it binding, not merely a scheduling note: 'this spec and SPEC-TRACK3B2 (once drafted) constitute a single atomic release unit for any production-facing deployment. This spec's implementation must not be deployed to, or merged ahead of SPEC-TRACK3B2 in, any environment where `callisto matrix` or `callisto publish` runs against a real workspace, until SPEC-TRACK3B2's matrix.rs/publish.rs collision-safety fix has landed in the same release.' This spec is that fix, and the same atomicity constraint applies symmetrically in the other direction: this spec's own acceptance criteria (which require constructing a workspace fixture with two promoted PackageId::Prefixed siblings sharing a bare name) cannot be exercised against a real walk until SPEC-TRACK3B1's walk.rs promotion logic has actually landed -- not merely because the PackageId::Prefixed variant, PackageId::display_name(), PackageId::resolve_unique, or aggregate.rs's resolve_target_package/GraphError::AmbiguousName pattern are missing from the codebase (all four were verified present and already in use elsewhere -- e.g. crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:575-608 already constructs PackageId::Prefixed values for registry dispatch, and crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:153-162 already implements the resolve_target_package/AmbiguousName pattern this spec reuses, with existing ambiguity tests at aggregate.rs:997-1090) -- but because today's walk.rs still rejects any same-bare-name, cross-ecosystem, different-path pair with GraphError::DuplicatePackage at discovery time, so no workspace can ever produce two registered packages sharing a bare name for this spec's new code paths to exercise until that rejection is replaced by promotion. Implementation of this spec's acceptance criteria therefore requires SPEC-TRACK3B1's walk.rs change to have already landed, even though the library primitives this spec's fix reuses do not themselves require it.
scope:

crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs: `MatrixOptions.package: Option<String>` (lines 9-14) and `matrix()` (lines 16-55). Its existence check at line 23 (`!all_packages.iter().any(|p| p.id.name() == name)`) and its filter closure at lines 32-37 (`p.id.name() == n`) both currently match by bare name only, with no ambiguity detection -- given two promoted siblings sharing a bare name, both currently pass the existence check and both currently pass the filter, so `--package <name>` silently includes both siblings' data in one report. In scope: replace both the existence check and the filter with a single ambiguity-aware resolution, reusing the exact pattern already implemented at crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:153-162 (`pub(crate) fn resolve_target_package<'a>(packages: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Package>, id: &PackageId) -> Result<Option<&'a Package>, GraphError>`, which calls `id.resolve_unique(packages, |p| &p.id)` and maps an ambiguous result to `Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName { name: id.display_name(), candidates })`) -- `resolve_target_package` is `pub(crate)` in the same crate (callisto_graph), so commands/matrix.rs can call it directly via `crate::aggregate::resolve_target_package`. `opts.package`'s string is parsed via `PackageId::parse` (crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:24-81, already ecosystem-prefix-aware for both `cargo:name` and `cargo/name` forms) before being passed to `resolve_target_package`, so an operator may pass either a bare name (ambiguity-checked) or an explicit ecosystem-qualified name (`cargo/native-core`) to disambiguate directly.

crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs: `PublishOptions.only: Vec<String>` (lines 12-17) and its filter logic inside `plan_publish` at lines 437-462 -- the `keep` closure (line 438, `|name: &str| opts.only.iter().any(|n| n == name)`) and its five `.retain()` call sites (lines 439-443: `rust_crates`, `npm_main_packages`, `npm_platform_packages`, `pypi_packages`, each filtered by `c.name` -- a bare `String` field on `CratePublish`/`NpmMainPublish`/`NpmPublish`/`PypiPublish`, confirmed against crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:44-137, none of which carry a `PackageId` field, only `name: String` -- and `releases`, filtered by `r.package.name()`, where `ReleaseEntry.package: PackageId` (plan.rs:112) DOES carry the full identity). In scope: for each name in `opts.only`, resolve it exactly once via `PackageId::parse` + `resolve_target_package(ws.graph.packages(), &parsed_id)` before any list filtering begins, surfacing `Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName)` immediately (via `?`) for any ambiguous bare name, and `Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage)` for any name matching zero registered packages. Each successfully resolved name yields one concrete `PackageId` (Bare or Prefixed). Because `rust_crates` is exclusively Cargo-ecosystem, `npm_main_packages`/`npm_platform_packages` exclusively Npm-ecosystem, and `pypi_packages` exclusively Pypi-ecosystem (each list is populated from a single-ecosystem `PublishTarget` dispatch branch, verified at publish.rs:206-411), each list's own `.retain()` predicate is scoped to keep an entry only when some resolved id's name matches AND (for a `Prefixed` resolved id) that id's ecosystem matches the list's fixed ecosystem -- a `Bare` resolved id (the unambiguous, unpromoted case) keeps matching on name alone, identical to today's behavior. `releases`' retain is scoped using `PackageId::matches()` (identity.rs:148-160) against each resolved id directly, since `ReleaseEntry.package` already carries a full `PackageId`.

CORRECTION (round 2 audit, blocker 3): the existing post-hoc `retained`-set validation at publish.rs:445-461 does NOT become redundant and is NOT removed. It enforces a distinct invariant this spec must preserve: `resolve_target_package` only checks whether the resolved `PackageId` exists in the full registered-package graph (`ws.graph.packages()`), independent of publish eligibility (non-empty `publish_to`, not all `PublishTarget::None`, has a dispatchable target). A registered-but-not-eligible package (e.g. a docs-only crate with an empty `publish_to`) resolves `Ok(Some(pkg))` from `resolve_target_package` but never contributed an entry to `rust_crates`/`npm_main_packages`/`npm_platform_packages`/`pypi_packages`/`releases` in the first place -- today's code catches exactly this case via the `retained`-set check and returns `Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage)`; silently dropping that check would let such a name resolve successfully and produce a plan where it contributes nothing, with no error. In scope: re-source the existing eligibility check from each surviving entry's OWN real `pkg.id`, not from a re-derived `PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: <the list's fixed ecosystem>, name: c.name.clone()}` construction, because a package's registry-target ecosystem (which list it lands in -- `rust_crates` for CratesIo, `npm_main_packages`/`npm_platform_packages` for Npm, `pypi_packages` for Pypi, driven purely by the package's OWN CONFIGURED `PublishTarget` dispatch at publish.rs:206-411) is not provably identical to the package's own `PackageId` ecosystem (which comes from the package's manifest kind, post-SPEC-TRACK3B1). These two ecosystems happen to coincide for every fixture this spec constructs, but re-deriving identity from the list's fixed ecosystem rather than from the package's own `pkg.id` silently assumes they always coincide, which is not proven anywhere in real code (see the divergence non-goal below). The corrected mechanism (CORRECTION, round 4 audit, blocker 1 -- the original "filter the side Vec<PackageId> by index/name correlation" wording was not mechanically implementable: Vec::retain removes elements independently and records no dropped-index information, so post-hoc index correlation is impossible without extra structure, and name correlation is exactly the ambiguity hole AC-19 exists to catch, so it cannot be used either): build five parallel id-tracking vectors alongside the five existing lists, one per list -- `rust_crate_ids: Vec<PackageId>` alongside `rust_crates`, `npm_main_ids: Vec<PackageId>` alongside `npm_main_packages`, `npm_platform_ids: Vec<PackageId>` alongside `npm_platform_packages`, `pypi_ids: Vec<PackageId>` alongside `pypi_packages`, and `release_ids: Vec<PackageId>` alongside `releases` -- during the SAME dispatch loop at publish.rs:206-411, pushing each entry's originating `pkg.id.clone()` into the matching per-list id vector at the exact same push site (same iteration, same `if` branch) that pushes the corresponding `CratePublish`/`NpmMainPublish`/`NpmPublish`/`PypiPublish`/`ReleaseEntry` into its own list -- this does not widen `PublishPlan`'s serialized schema, since all five id vectors are build-local tracking structures internal to `plan_publish`, never serialized, never part of the returned `PublishPlan` struct. `release_ids` is included as a fifth per-list id vector (`r.package.clone()`, already a full `PackageId`), in addition to the four per-ecosystem id vectors; this is behavior-preserving relative to today's four-list-only `retained`-set check, verified against real code: `releases.push` (publish.rs:423, inside the `has_dispatchable_target` gate) only ever fires for a package that also set `has_dispatchable_target = true` via one of the `publishes_cargo`/`publishes_npm`/`publishes_pypi` branches (publish.rs:206-411), so any package identity present in `releases`/`release_ids` is already present in one of the four per-ecosystem lists -- adding `release_ids` as a fifth id vector cannot change which resolved ids find a surviving match, it only adds a redundant, harmless second path to the same match. Each of the five existing `.retain(pred)` calls (publish.rs:439-443) is replaced by a zip-retain-unzip: for each list, zip its entries together with its parallel id vector into one `Vec<(Entry, PackageId)>` (e.g. `rust_crates.into_iter().zip(rust_crate_ids).collect()`), call `.retain(|(entry, _)| pred(entry))` on the zipped vector -- the retain predicate still only inspects `entry`, unchanged in substance from today's `pred` -- then unzip the survivors back into the original entry list (`rust_crates`, reassigned) and its now-correspondingly-filtered id vector (`rust_crate_ids`, reassigned), and identically for the other four list/id-vector pairs (`npm_main_packages`/`npm_main_ids`, `npm_platform_packages`/`npm_platform_ids`, `pypi_packages`/`pypi_ids`, `releases`/`release_ids`). Because the zip pairs each entry with its id at the same index and retain only ever drops or keeps whole `(entry, id)` tuples together, the surviving id vector's contents correspond exactly, index-for-index, to the surviving entries -- no index or name correlation is performed after the fact. After all five zipped-retains complete, concatenate the five surviving per-list id vectors (`rust_crate_ids`, `npm_main_ids`, `npm_platform_ids`, `pypi_ids`, `release_ids`) into one flat `Vec<PackageId>` of surviving identities, then, for the first resolved id in the up-front resolution set (built earlier in this same function from `opts.only`) for which no surviving identity in that flat `Vec<PackageId>` satisfies `resolved_id.matches(&surviving_id)`, return `Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: resolved_id })`. This is deliberately NOT a raw name-string membership test: two promoted siblings can share a bare name across ecosystems, so testing whether the bare name string 'shared-lib' is present anywhere in the five lists would let an ineligible sibling in one ecosystem (e.g. `npm/shared-lib`, empty `publish_to`, contributes to none of the five lists) hide behind an eligible, differently-scoped sibling of the same bare name (`cargo/shared-lib`, present in `rust_crates`) requested in the same `--only` invocation -- silently passing the ineligible sibling's `--only` entry with no error. Reconstructing full `PackageId`s from each entry's own real `pkg.id` and matching via `PackageId::matches()` closes exactly that hole, and does so correctly even in the (unfixtured) divergent-ecosystem case, since the side vector captures each entry's true identity rather than re-deriving it from list membership. See AC-17, AC-18, and AC-19.

Handling the case where a promoted package's registry-target ecosystem (which of rust_crates/npm_main_packages/npm_platform_packages/pypi_packages it lands in, driven purely by its own configured PublishTarget dispatch at publish.rs:206-411) diverges from its own PackageId ecosystem (driven by its manifest kind, post-SPEC-TRACK3B1) -- e.g. a package whose primary manifest is Cargo.toml (PackageId::Prefixed{Cargo, name}) but whose [[package]] publish_to override (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs's PackageConfig.publish_to, verified this session to accept any PublishTarget value independent of the package's manifest kind, with no cross-validation tying the two) configures publish_to = ["npm"], causing the package to be dispatched into npm_main_packages/npm_platform_packages while its own true identity remains Prefixed{Cargo, name}. This spec's `.retain()` step for each of the four per-ecosystem lists keeps an entry when a resolved --only id's name matches AND, for a Prefixed resolved id, that id's ecosystem matches the LIST's fixed ecosystem (the ecosystem the list represents, not necessarily the surviving entry's own true PackageId ecosystem) -- for a divergent package this retain predicate would incorrectly exclude the entry before this spec's corrected eligibility check (see scope) ever runs, since the eligibility check's side-vector fix only corrects the post-retain reconstruction, not the retain predicate itself. Correctly handling this divergence would require replacing the retain step's list-fixed-ecosystem heuristic with a lookup against the same per-list id vectors (rust_crate_ids/npm_main_ids/npm_platform_ids/pypi_ids/release_ids) the eligibility-check fix captures at push time -- a change to the retain step itself, not merely the post-hoc eligibility check this spec's blocker-3 fix addresses. This spec does not construct a fixture for this divergent case and does not fix the retain step's heuristic, because doing so is a larger, structurally distinct change than the eligibility-check reconstruction fix this spec makes, and no evidence was found that this divergence occurs in the actual workspace today; deferred to a follow-on spec if a real divergent configuration is ever observed.

api_surface.name: MatrixOptions::package resolution (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs)
api_surface.signature: pub fn matrix<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, opts: &MatrixOptions) -> Result<MatrixReport, GraphError>
api_surface.description: Unchanged signature and unchanged `Ok` behavior for every currently-passing case. Internal behavior change: when `opts.package` is `Some(raw)`, `raw` is parsed via `PackageId::parse(raw)`. When parsing succeeds, the resulting `PackageId` (Bare or Prefixed) is used as `resolved_id` directly. When `PackageId::parse(raw)` returns `Err` (e.g. `raw` contains `..`, starts with `/` or `-`, or has an empty name after a recognised ecosystem prefix), `matrix()` falls back to constructing `resolved_id = PackageId::Bare(raw.clone())` and proceeds exactly as if that `Bare` id had been the parse result -- no separate parse-error branch or panic. `resolved_id` is then resolved via `crate::aggregate::resolve_target_package(all_packages.iter().copied(), &resolved_id)`. Because no registered package can ever equal a malformed bare string (registered packages are never constructed from raw, unvalidated `--package` input), this fallback deterministically yields `Ok(None)` from `resolve_target_package`, which `matrix()` maps to `Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: resolved_id })` -- identical to today's behavior for any `--package` value that matches no registered package, whether or not it fails `PackageId::parse`. `Ok(Some(pkg))` restricts the report to `pkg.id`; `Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName { name, candidates })` propagates via `?` unmodified from `resolve_target_package`. The filter closure previously at matrix.rs:32-37 (`p.id.name() == n`) is replaced by a `p.id.matches(&resolved_id)` check (via `PackageId::matches()`, identity.rs:148-160) rather than exact PackageId equality. `.matches()` is used here -- not structural equality -- because it makes the filter step correct independent of any assumption about SPEC-TRACK3B1's promotion invariants, consistent with every other identity comparison this spec's own publish.rs fix performs via PackageId::matches() (see PublishOptions::only resolution, releases.retain()'s predicate) rather than equality. The existence check and the filter share the same resolved id and the same `.matches()` semantics, so they can never disagree. See AC-16.

api_surface.name: PublishOptions::only resolution (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs)
api_surface.signature: pub fn plan_publish<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, opts: &PublishOptions) -> Result<PublishPlan, GraphError>
api_surface.description: Unchanged signature and unchanged `Ok` behavior for every currently-passing case. Internal behavior change: immediately before the `if !opts.only.is_empty()` block (publish.rs:437), each `name` in `opts.only` is parsed via `PackageId::parse(name)`. When parsing succeeds, the resulting `PackageId` is used directly; when `PackageId::parse(name)` returns `Err`, resolution falls back to constructing `PackageId::Bare(name.clone())` and proceeds exactly as if that `Bare` id had been the parse result -- identical fallback pattern to `MatrixOptions::package` resolution above. For each name in opts.only, `crate::aggregate::resolve_target_package(ws.graph.packages(), &resolved_id)` is called once, per its real signature `fn resolve_target_package<'a>(packages: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Package>, id: &PackageId) -> Result<Option<&'a Package>, GraphError>` (aggregate.rs:153-162) -- not a batch call returning `Result<Vec<PackageId>, GraphError>`. Iterating opts.only and calling resolve_target_package once per name, collecting each `Ok(Some(pkg))` into a `Vec<PackageId>` of `pkg.id.clone()` (the up-front resolution set the later eligibility check consumes), propagating the first `Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName)` via `?` immediately -- aborting before any list is filtered or any registry call is made -- and returning `Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: resolved_id })` for the first name whose call returns `Ok(None)` (a malformed name, e.g. `../etc`, deterministically falls into this branch since no registered package can equal a malformed bare string -- see AC-18). Each of `rust_crates`/`npm_main_packages`/`npm_platform_packages`/`pypi_packages`'s `.retain()` predicate keeps an entry when some resolved id's `.name()` equals the entry's `.name` field AND, if that resolved id is `PackageId::Prefixed`, its `.ecosystem()` matches the list's fixed ecosystem (Cargo for rust_crates; Npm for both npm lists; Pypi for pypi_packages) -- a `PackageId::Bare` resolved id keeps matching by name alone, unchanged from today. `releases.retain()`'s predicate becomes `resolved.iter().any(|id| id.matches(&r.package))`, using `PackageId::matches()` directly since `ReleaseEntry.package` already carries a full `PackageId`. After these five `.retain()` calls (CORRECTION, round 4 audit, blocker 1: not plain `.retain()` calls on the entry lists alone -- see the zip-retain-unzip mechanism below, which is what actually produces both the filtered entry lists and their correspondingly-filtered id vectors in one step), the pre-existing eligibility check (publish.rs:445-461) is retained in substance and re-sourced from each surviving entry's OWN real `pkg.id`, captured via five parallel id-tracking vectors built alongside the five existing lists during the same dispatch loop (publish.rs:206-411) -- `rust_crate_ids`, `npm_main_ids`, `npm_platform_ids`, `pypi_ids`, and `release_ids`, each a `Vec<PackageId>`. Each surviving entry's originating `pkg.id.clone()` is pushed into the matching per-list id vector at the exact push site its corresponding `CratePublish`/`NpmMainPublish`/`NpmPublish`/`PypiPublish`/`ReleaseEntry` is pushed into its own list. These five id vectors are build-local tracking structures, never serialized as part of `PublishPlan`, so this does not widen `PublishPlan`'s schema. Each of the five existing `.retain(pred)` calls is replaced by a zip-retain-unzip: zip the list with its parallel id vector into a single `Vec<(Entry, PackageId)>`, call `.retain(|(entry, _)| pred(entry))` on the zipped vector (the predicate still only inspects `entry`, unchanged in substance from today), then unzip the survivors back into the original entry list and its now-correspondingly-filtered id vector -- since retain drops or keeps each `(entry, id)` tuple as a unit, the surviving id vector matches the surviving entries exactly, index-for-index, with no correlation performed after the fact. `release_ids` contributes a fifth id vector (`r.package.clone()`, already a full `PackageId`); this is behavior-preserving relative to today's four-list-only check because `releases.push` only ever fires for a package that also set `has_dispatchable_target = true` via one of the four per-ecosystem dispatch branches, so every identity in `releases`/`release_ids` already appears in one of the four per-ecosystem lists. Deliberately NOT reconstructed as `PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem: <the list's fixed ecosystem>, name: c.name.clone() }`, because a surviving entry's registry-target ecosystem (which list it landed in, driven by its own configured `PublishTarget`) is not provably identical to its own `PackageId` ecosystem (driven by its manifest kind) -- re-deriving from list membership silently assumes they always coincide, which this spec does not fixture or prove (see this spec's non_goals). After all five zipped-retains complete, the five surviving per-list id vectors are concatenated into one flat `Vec<PackageId>` of surviving identities, and this check returns `Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: resolved_id })` for the first resolved id in the up-front resolution set for which no surviving identity in that flat vector satisfies `resolved_id.matches(&surviving_id)`. This is deliberately NOT a raw name-string membership test against the five lists: two promoted siblings can share a bare name across ecosystems (e.g. `cargo/shared-lib`, eligible, present in `rust_crates`; `npm/shared-lib`, registered but ineligible with an empty `publish_to`, present in none of the five lists), so a name-only check would let `npm/shared-lib`'s `--only` entry silently pass with no error by matching on the bare name string 'shared-lib' contributed by the unrelated eligible `cargo/shared-lib` entry -- reconstructing each entry's true `PackageId` from its own captured `pkg.id` and comparing via `PackageId::matches()` (ecosystem-aware) closes that hole, since `npm/shared-lib`'s resolved id matches no `Prefixed{Cargo, 'shared-lib'}` surviving identity. This check covers a registered-but-not-publish-eligible package (e.g. empty `publish_to`), which `resolve_target_package` alone cannot detect since it only checks graph membership, not eligibility. See AC-17, AC-18, and AC-19.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a workspace where SPEC-TRACK3B1's promotion has produced two registered packages sharing the bare name "native-core", with each path's manifests and declared names spelled out explicitly: (1) crates/native-core/Cargo.toml declares package.name = "native-core" -- the only manifest at that path claiming the name "native-core", so this path's claiming-ecosystem set for "native-core" is {Cargo}; a co-located crates/native-core/package.json exists solely to carry napi.targets = ["aarch64-apple-darwin"] but declares name = "native-core-napi" -- a DIFFERENT name from the colliding "native-core" -- so it contributes nothing to "native-core"'s claiming-ecosystem set. (2) packages/native-core/package.json declares name = "native-core" -- the only manifest at that path claiming the name "native-core", so this path's claiming-ecosystem set for "native-core" is {Npm}; a co-located packages/native-core/pyproject.toml exists solely to carry [tool.maturin].targets = ["aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"] but declares project.name = "native-core-py" -- a different name -- so it contributes nothing to "native-core"'s claiming-ecosystem set. "native-core"'s two claiming-ecosystem sets are therefore {Cargo} and {Npm}, which are disjoint, satisfying SPEC-TRACK3B1 AC-21's promotion precondition (disjoint name-scoped claiming-ecosystem sets), so the two packages promote to PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Cargo, name: "native-core"} and PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Npm, name: "native-core"} respectively. Running `callisto matrix --format json` produces a platformTargets object containing exactly two keys, "cargo/native-core" and "npm/native-core", each with its own correct kind/source/targets, neither entry silently overwritten by the other.

Given the same two-package fixture as AC-01 (identical manifests, paths, and declared names), the Npm sibling's existing packages/native-core/package.json additionally declares engines.node, and a new packages/native-core/pyproject.toml-equivalent is not needed since requires-python is instead added via a new crates/native-core/pyproject.toml declaring requires-python but project.name = "native-core-cli-py" -- again a different name from "native-core", so it does not add Pypi to "native-core"'s claiming-ecosystem set and the AC-01 disjointness analysis ({Cargo} vs {Npm}) is unaffected; this new file carries no [tool.maturin].targets, so it does not trigger matrix.rs's napi/maturin same-directory hard error. `callisto matrix --format json`'s runtimeVersions object likewise contains exactly two keys, "cargo/native-core" and "npm/native-core", each with its own correct entries.

In a workspace with no promoted collisions (every registered package has a distinct bare name, all PackageId::Bare), running `callisto matrix --format json` produces platformTargets/runtimeVersions keys identical to the bare package names -- byte-identical output to the pre-this-spec behavior -- since PackageId::display_name() returns the bare name unchanged for PackageId::Bare.

Given the AC-01 fixture, running `callisto matrix --package native-core --format json` (the ambiguous bare name, matching both promoted siblings) exits with a non-zero code via GraphError::AmbiguousName, and prints an error message naming "native-core" as ambiguous and listing both candidate identities (cargo/native-core, npm/native-core); no MatrixReport JSON is printed to stdout.

Given the AC-01 fixture, running `callisto matrix --package cargo/native-core --format json` (the fully ecosystem-qualified name) exits 0 and produces a MatrixReport containing only the Cargo sibling's platformTargets/runtimeVersions entry (keyed "cargo/native-core"), with the Npm sibling's entry absent from both maps.

In a workspace with no promoted collisions, running `callisto matrix --package <name>` where <name> is exactly one registered (unpromoted, Bare) package's bare name behaves identically to today: the report is restricted to that one package, and `callisto matrix --package does-not-exist` still exits non-zero via GraphError::UnknownPackage naming "does-not-exist".

Given a workspace where SPEC-TRACK3B1's promotion has produced two registered packages sharing the bare name "shared-lib" -- PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Cargo, name: "shared-lib"} (its own single manifest is Cargo.toml, publish_to = ["crates-io"]), and PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Npm, name: "shared-lib"} (its own single manifest is package.json, publish_to = ["npm"]) -- calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["shared-lib".to_string()] })` (the ambiguous bare name) returns Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName { name, candidates }) with name == "shared-lib" and candidates containing both siblings' PackageIds, and no Ok(PublishPlan) value is ever returned from this call -- callers cannot observe a partial or filtered PublishPlan for this input under any circumstance, only the Err. (CORRECTION, round 4 audit, blocker 2: this criterion no longer asserts that the five ecosystem lists are unbuilt at the point of the error -- per this spec's own scope section, the dispatch loop at publish.rs:206-411 fully populates rust_crates/npm_main_packages/npm_platform_packages/pypi_packages/releases as internal, un-returned local variables before the up-front --only resolution's AmbiguousName check runs; whether those internal locals exist at any given moment inside plan_publish is a private implementation detail, not observable from outside the function's Result<PublishPlan, GraphError> signature, so this criterion only asserts the one thing an external caller actually can observe: the call returns Err, never a partial or filtered Ok(PublishPlan).)

Given the AC-07 fixture, calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["cargo/shared-lib".to_string()] })` (fully ecosystem-qualified) returns Ok(PublishPlan) whose rust_crates contains exactly one entry with name == "shared-lib", and whose npm_main_packages and npm_platform_packages are both empty -- the Npm sibling is excluded even though its bare name is identical.

Given the AC-07 fixture, calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["npm/shared-lib".to_string()] })` returns Ok(PublishPlan) whose npm_main_packages or npm_platform_packages (whichever role applies to the fixture's Npm sibling) contains exactly one entry with name == "shared-lib", and whose rust_crates is empty -- the Cargo sibling is excluded.

In a workspace with no promoted collisions, calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec![name.to_string()] })` where `name` is exactly one registered (unpromoted, PackageId::Bare) package's bare name behaves identically to today: the returned Ok(PublishPlan) is restricted to that one package's ecosystem-appropriate list(s), and calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["does-not-exist".to_string()] })` still returns Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: PackageId::Bare("does-not-exist".to_string()) }).

Given the AC-07 fixture, both siblings additionally configured to produce a ReleaseEntry (a release-eligible version bump for each), calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["cargo/shared-lib".to_string()] })` returns Ok(PublishPlan) whose `releases` list contains exactly one entry, whose `package` field equals the Cargo sibling's PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Cargo, name: "shared-lib"}, with the Npm sibling's ReleaseEntry absent.

crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs's MatrixReport doc comment no longer states that map keys are ordered by 'registered package name (PackageId::name())' -- it states keys are PackageId::display_name(), ordered lexicographically by that string, and crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs's build_matrix_report doc comment no longer states 'Map keys are each package's bare name' -- it likewise states display_name().

crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs's MatrixOptions.package doc comment and crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs's PublishOptions.only doc comment each state that an ambiguous bare name (matching two or more promoted siblings) returns Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName), and that an ecosystem-qualified name (e.g. "cargo/name") disambiguates directly -- neither doc comment asserts pure, unqualified bare-name matching as the complete contract any longer.

In .claude/specs/track-g-matrix-napi-maturin.json, the AC-006 and AC-009 acceptance_criteria entries' `criterion` fields no longer state that --package matching or platformTargets/runtimeVersions key ordering uses 'PackageId::name() ... not display_name()' -- both are edited to state PackageId::display_name() is the map-key and --package-match format, consistent with this spec's AC-01/AC-04/AC-05. Every other field of both objects (id, is_error_case) and every other acceptance_criteria entry in the file remain byte-identical to their pre-edit values.

Every pre-existing test in crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs's #[cfg(test)] module (verified this session: build_matrix_report_empty_workspace_produces_empty_report, build_matrix_report_orders_packages_lexicographically, build_matrix_report_dual_manifest_runtime_versions_npm_before_python, build_matrix_report_single_file_serves_both_platform_and_runtime_extraction, and every other test in that module) passes unmodified after this spec's rekey lands, since all of them construct only PackageId::Bare fixtures via the existing pkg_id/input helpers.

Running `callisto matrix --package ../etc` (a string that fails PackageId::parse due to the `..` path-traversal check) exits non-zero via GraphError::UnknownPackage naming "../etc", not a panic, not an unhandled parse-error variant, and not a silently empty report.

Given a workspace where a registered package named "docs-only" declares an empty publish_to (i.e. it is registered but not publish-eligible: it never appears in rust_crates, npm_main_packages, npm_platform_packages, pypi_packages, or releases), calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["docs-only".to_string()] })` returns Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: PackageId::Bare("docs-only".to_string()) }) -- identical to today's behavior -- not a silently empty or partial Ok(PublishPlan).

Calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["../etc".to_string()] })` (a string that fails PackageId::parse due to the `..` path-traversal check, and therefore falls back to PackageId::Bare("../etc".to_string()) per this spec's resolution-fallback mechanism) returns Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: PackageId::Bare("../etc".to_string()) }), not a panic, not an unhandled parse-error variant, and not a silently empty or partial Ok(PublishPlan).

Given a workspace where SPEC-TRACK3B1's promotion has produced two registered packages sharing the bare name "shared-lib" -- PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Cargo, name: "shared-lib"} configured with publish_to = ["crates-io"] (publish-eligible, contributes an entry to rust_crates), and PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem: Npm, name: "shared-lib"} configured with an empty publish_to (registered but not publish-eligible: contributes no entry to any of rust_crates/npm_main_packages/npm_platform_packages/pypi_packages/releases) -- calling `plan_publish(&ws, &PublishOptions { only: vec!["cargo/shared-lib".to_string(), "npm/shared-lib".to_string()] })` in a single call returns Err(GraphError::UnknownPackage { id: PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem: Ecosystem::Npm, name: "shared-lib".to_string() } }), not Ok(PublishPlan) with rust_crates containing the Cargo sibling and the Npm sibling silently omitted with no error. This confirms the eligibility check reconstructs full PackageId identities (via the side Vec<PackageId> captured at push time, see scope) and matches via PackageId::matches() rather than testing raw bare-name-string membership across the five lists -- a raw-name-string check would find "shared-lib" present (contributed by the unrelated eligible Cargo entry) and incorrectly let the ineligible Npm sibling's --only entry pass with no error.
